shared: Frozen November 18 at 14:29:59 UTC before the US regular open. D1 is the November 18 regular session. P0 is the November 17 regular close for each issuer. SMH closed at 460.10, down 5.6% since November 9, and QQQ at 656.95, down 3.3%; the common selloff weakens any claim that a single issuer caused the move. Nvidia reported after the November 17 21:00 UTC regular close. The November 17 21:38 UTC archived release coverage, first seen by 23:00 UTC, reports $115.8bn revenue and a $130bn outlook. Coverage at 21:41-21:53 UTC reports an above-consensus outlook and an initial stock rise. Those headlines preceded the cutoff, but the regular-session OHLC ends before the release. Treat the after-hours response as qualitative and await regular-session acceptance. This provides evidence for current AI infrastructure demand, while persistent upside requires guidance to convert into funded orders. Reuters pre-report market coverage and Anthropic debut attention establish context without an IPO outcome (N-d6cc48d72f0659e7, N-3011030f3d738952). Six observed close-to-close moves and seven intraday ranges provide a scale, with too little history for stable volatility inference. Conditional USD closing-price estimates use the observed swing levels and roughly one to two ordinary session moves for early repricing, then assume partial mean reversion in the central paths and multi-session follow-through in the tails. Probabilities are judgmental, and common catalysts can correlate outcomes across names. The opposing opening cites $108.85bn in pre-release quarterly revenue consensus (N-0f4ff70563975d1a), making the reported result a 6.4% beat. That comparator applies to the reported quarter. The forward guide was characterized as above expectations in the archive, with no directly comparable numeric forward consensus. The shared return found no funded-order, licensing or supplier schedule breakdown. Unknown allocations limit any increase in conviction in either direction. The archive schedules the Anthropic listing for Thursday, November 19 (D2), a prospective financing-sentiment test (N-8cb6b8b2235b7aed).

MU.thesis: P0 $712.42. Mild downside skew. The 12.2% giveback from the November 11 close and November 17 recovery from $666.88 make a fresh sell case depend on earnings exposure beyond the existing selloff. A NAND price forecast cut raises the risk of lower realized storage pricing if additional supply arrives ahead of demand. The 2027 warning matters here only if estimates adjust within 15 sessions. A refusal to dismiss DRAM litigation adds headline sensitivity, with no finding of liability in the archived report. The prior $778-$811 closing area and the last session low frame the tails; daily close-return sample SD was 6.5% and average high-low range was 6.2% of close.
MU.counterevidence: The archive reports tight AI memory availability and a shipping Micron design win in Oxide servers, with purchase volume unspecified. Nvidia guidance supports accelerator-linked memory demand if the production outlook converts to HBM orders. NAND pressure leaves that HBM channel open. The November 17 lower wick shows recovery from the low before Nvidia reported.
MU.falsifier: Corroborated firm near-term NAND contract pricing or HBM allocation gains sufficient to offset a projected NAND margin decline would remove the downside skew. A sustained close above the November 13 close near $778 following those revisions would support follow-through.
MU.opponent_response: I agree that a higher HBM mix could finance a recovery toward the November 13 close, and the shipping Oxide design is stronger evidence of an actual deployment than a hypothetical customer win. The disclosed system gives no scale against MU storage exposure. The same tight-memory article flags a major buyer potentially developing a rival, which makes the absence of cut-through to Micron allocations particularly consequential. GF Securities offers a forward NAND price thesis and the lawsuit raises headline exposure, but neither measures a near-term margin hit. Compared with TSM, the mix of memory technologies and supplier allocations creates an extra filter between accelerator demand and issuer economics. This supports a broad upside branch and a center near P0. The evidence for tilting toward HBM-led upside remains limited.
MU.revision: Retain all three paths and weights. The 32% storage-reset tail and 22% memory-pricing upside tail imply a nearly flat D15 probability-weighted close of $708.70. The small downside skew comes from the possibility that storage estimate cuts arrive faster than a verified HBM offset, with no new volume evidence to widen it.

NVDA.thesis: P0 $155.46. The ticker lost 13.0% since November 9 versus SMH down 5.6%, leaving room for a rebound on the disclosed beat and raise. The post-release report of a rise favors a higher early center. For D15 I retain a wider downside tail: leadership disruption can affect customer commitments and demand visibility if confidence in delivery or financing weakens. The archive lacks current exposure and bookings detail needed to assign a large directional edge. Six daily close moves had 3.1% sample SD against a 6.1% average intraday range; the $148.80 recent low and $173.73 November 11 close anchor the early tails, with further distance conditional on sustained revisions.
NVDA.counterevidence: Above-consensus forward guidance is direct evidence against an immediate demand collapse. The downside remains plausible if the upgrade was narrower than headline numbers imply or becomes harder to finance. Reuters reports that Huang is open to a return and a December congressional appearance. Those headlines leave leadership resolution uncertain.
NVDA.falsifier: Broad increases in forward estimates backed by disclosed customer funding and firm orders, alongside regular-session acceptance above the November 13 high near $170, would materially shrink the downside tail. Guidance support would fade if those revisions were reversed on disclosed order or financing weakness.
NVDA.opponent_response: The quarterly beat is measurable and belongs in the near-term price estimate for NVDA first. The opponent puts 40% on durable demand and cash execution, while I give the middle branch more weight because a beat and a qualitative after-hours rise warrant partial repricing before the incremental guide is reconciled. Financing commentary concerns some smaller cloud customers. It establishes a mechanism for collection risk, with no measured share of the $130bn guide or evidence that collections deteriorated. I therefore retain meaningful upside and avoid increasing the financing downside weight. Unlike AMD or AVGO, Nvidia has a direct issuer revenue surprise. Unlike MU or TSM, Nvidia also bears the first-order cash collection risk.
NVDA.revision: Retain all three paths and weights. The archived consensus quantifies a surprise that the opening already priced into the initial partial rebound. It sharpens the case for that branch without independently confirming forward cash execution or leadership risk. The $158.94 weighted D15 close allows a modest lift from P0 even with a wider downside tail.

AMD.thesis: P0 $503.41. Modest downside skew. The November 12 close of $585.30 was 15.1% above November 9 and lost 14.0% by November 17, so much of the local rerating already reversed. The remaining risk is that licensing delays defer a portion of accelerator shipments to certain affected customers and that Nvidia demand strength comes with fewer AMD share gains than expected. The archive lacks a quantified AMD exposure bridge. The $480.50 November 17 low and $534.06 November 13 close frame early paths, with 6.3% daily close-return SD and a 7.5% average range.
AMD.counterevidence: The same Nvidia guide can signal a larger industry order pool. Commentary about a higher CPU share in AI systems supports a separate server CPU channel, without quantifying AMD wins. A leadership transition also creates openings for rival accelerators if customers diversify. That possibility warrants a rebound branch while the archive lacks bookings or confirmed share shifts.
AMD.falsifier: Firm AMD accelerator order conversions or licensing clearance protecting shipment timing, paired with a verified server CPU estimate raise, would materially weaken the downside case. A sustained close above $534 would support the market acceptance of such a revision.

paths.label: Deployment deferrals or weaker share capture
CPU and AI demand absorb drag
Accelerator wins and server CPU upgrade

AMD.opponent_response: I agree that larger accelerator budgets could support a second source and that the Nvidia beat primarily demonstrates incumbent sales execution. The same budget can expand overall and still bypass AMD, whereas an AMD server CPU win could add demand regardless of GPU share. AVGO custom programs provide a useful comparison because they can draw on a distinct hyperscaler procurement route. The archived licensing headline is specific to certain customers and jurisdictions, and does not quantify AMD exposure. With the local rally already reversed, the absence of second-source orders limits the upside lean and the absence of measured licensing losses limits the downside lean.
AMD.revision: Retain all three paths and weights. These are close to hold in aggregate, at $500.60 by D15. Keep a mildly heavier downside tail for combined deferral and share-capture risks, with no fresh evidence to deepen it or to upgrade the second-source branch.

AVGO.thesis: P0 $341.60. Hold around this price. AVGO retained a 6.9% gain since November 9 against the SMH decline and rose on November 17 while SMH fell, leaving room for relative gains to unwind if diversification into custom chips gets ahead of committed deployments. Nvidia guidance can support complement demand for networking and at the same time pressure the relative case for custom silicon share gains. The $330.13 recent low and $364.36 November 12 close anchor the early paths, against 4.4% close-return SD and a 4.6% average range.
AVGO.counterevidence: Archived coverage points to custom AI accelerators and networking growth. Custom accelerator demand depends on customer programs and networking can also benefit from expanding clusters built around merchant GPUs. The coverage gives limited detail on incremental committed volume or timing, which restrains both the bullish inference and an outright short view.
AVGO.falsifier: A disclosed customer-backed custom silicon ramp with scheduled volume or a measurable AI networking backlog increase would undercut the unwind thesis. A sustained close above $364 following a corroborated estimate raise would support the upside path.

paths.label: Custom deployments slip and relative bid fades

AVGO.opponent_response: I agree with the distinction between TPU and networking demand and with the evidence that AVGO traded differently than its peers before the report. The relative bid is compatible with some diversification already being priced. It offers little basis to raise the probability of a funded TPU program or a Broadcom networking win. The Nvidia beat has a plausible complementary effect through cluster networking, whereas TPU volumes require their own customer program and network content still depends on AVGO winning the socket. Relative strength versus AMD helps identify different pricing behavior while leaving the two companies with distinct procurement tests. Concentrated customer programs can delay both channels and provide a meaningful downside branch.
AVGO.revision: Retain all three paths and weights. The shared return adds no committed volume or timing to justify the opponent?s 35% dual-expansion branch. The weighted D15 close of $344.70 remains close to P0 with slightly more distance in the upside tail.

TSM.thesis: P0 $359.69. Hold with a wide tail on each side. TSM fell 13.0% from its November 11 close and underperformed SMH since November 9. October record sales establish recent strength and were reported days before the latest selloff, so the decline provides little evidence about reception to a fresh sales surprise. ADR downside can persist if the Nvidia transition or an AI capex funding shock delays orders enough to leave advanced node or packaging slots idle. The archive does not establish such a delay. A $353.50 November 17 low, $373.45 prior close, and $398.73 November 13 close scale the paths against 3.8% daily close-return SD and a 3.8% average range.
TSM.counterevidence: Strong recent sales and Nvidia guidance support utilization. TSM may capture foundry and packaging spend from alternative customers and chip designs if market share shifts. This offsets single-customer uncertainty if workloads still grow and the capacity slots are transferable. Aggregate revenue and an accelerator guide give limited information about allocation through the forecast window.
TSM.falsifier: Evidence that advanced-node wafer starts and packaging bookings remain firm across major customers, with alternative volumes taking up any displaced slots on schedule, would weaken the idle-capacity premise. A sustained close above $373.45 on a corroborated booking update would support repricing.
TSM.opponent_response: I accept the broader utilization case across multiple designers and the strong October sales base. Relative to AMD, TSM can still capture some leading-edge wafer demand when accelerator share shifts. Relative to MU, utilization across designs reduces dependence on a single memory allocation. Whether an available advanced packaging slot can be reassigned in time depends on the design, qualification and dates. The aggregate sales report and Nvidia beat do not resolve that question or the extent of the ADR risk discount. The November 17 close in the lower third of the range shows limited recovery before the report. It gives no evidence of how the ADR accepted the guide itself.
TSM.revision: Retain all three paths and weights. The record sales and guide keep the central path above P0. Confirmed replacement bookings would strengthen the upside case, while dated deferrals could deepen downside. With neither, the $362.56 weighted D15 close remains close to hold.
